scope: All 84 assigned person_2 records in 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel. Re-read current drafts/evidence, re-bound current SHA, checked primary witness excerpts against pinned WEB and source gates, and rechecked Wikipedia body-read support/relationship scope.
methodsJa: 引用節は固定WEBの同一book/chapter/verse本文・URLと照合した。
全プロフィールのsourceIds解決とfact/source knownByゲートをaudit-source-gates.pyで確認。
構造監査は0件で、意味的な同定承認とは分けた。
Wikipediaリンクは実記事本文のlocator/supportと現URL・現draft/profile SHAを照合。
全75リンクにcurrent body-read sidecarあり、本文内容は記事ページから再読。
profile wiki nullは検索済み根拠を確認し、未検索を記事不在と扱わない。
profile:nullは個人同定が固定WEBから支持されない場合の意図的除外として評価。
未解決canonical重複/別表記はqualifiedに保持。
現行draftのprimary source ID・citation URL・knownByを固定WEBの節座標へ照合し、profile SHAは契約のpretty JSON serialization（ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, terminal newline）で再計算した。
limitationsJa: 個人候補の一部は原文の地理/集団用法や異綴りとの関係が確定せず、profile:nullまたはqualifiedを維持した。
profile wiki nullの2SA God/Ephraimは検索済みだが、神学的同定または2SA2:9の人々/地域を特定する適合記事がない。
本 closure は独立レビューであり、公開・統合の承認ではない。
意味判定は先行する独立primary/Wikipedia実読記録と修正後の現行フィールドを再照合したclosureであり、このclosure自体は全84稿の新規全面的な独立記事再読を主張しない。
profile.sourceIdsの現行解決状況とprimary URLも全件機械照合した（解決漏れ0）。

factGates.textJa: アキシュの家臣たちは、ダビデがイスラエルの王だと歌われた人物ではないかと問い、ダビデは恐れました。
アキシュはダビデの振る舞いを見て、家臣たちに彼を連れて来た理由を問いました。
27章2節はアキシュをマオクの子と記します。本文だけでは、21章10節のアキシュと同一人物か、同名の別の王かは確定できません。
アキシュはダビデたちにガトでの居住を認め、後に地方の町を求めたダビデへツィクラグを与えました。
アキシュはダビデの説明を信じ、イスラエルの人々が彼を憎んだと考えました。
アキシュはダビデにペリシテ軍への参加を求め、ダビデを自分の護衛とすると述べました。
ペリシテ人の君主たちはダビデの同行に反対しました。アキシュはダビデの潔白を主張した後、彼らの意向に従って帰らせました。

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me, to bring me up?” Saul answered, “I am very distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God has departed from me, and answers me no more, by prophets, or by dreams. Therefore I have called you, that you may make known to me what I shall do.”
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then Saul fell immediately his full length on the earth, and was terrified, because of Samuel’s words. There was no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all day long or all night long.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: The woman came to Saul and saw that he was very troubled, and said to him, “Behold, your servant has listened to your voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have listened to your words which you spoke to me.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: She brought it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. Then they rose up and went away that night.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then the princes of the Philistines said, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish said to the princes of the Philistines, “Isn’t this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, who has been with me these days, or rather these years? I have found no fault in him since he fell away until today.”
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Isn’t this David, of whom people sang to one another in dances, saying, ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands’?”
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: The Philistines overtook Saul and his sons; and the Philistines killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: The battle went hard against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he was greatly distressed by reason of the archers.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then Saul said to his armor bearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through and abuse me!” But his armor bearer would not, for he was terrified. Therefore Saul took his sword and fell on it.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: When his armor bearer saw that Saul was dead, he likewise fell on his sword, and died with him.

factGates.textJa: サウルは預言者サムエルから油を注がれ、イスラエルの指導者として告げられました。
サウルはヤベシュ・ギレアデを救うため軍を集め、アンモン人を打ち破りました。
サムエルは、サウルが主の命令に従わなかったことを責め、王として退けられると告げました。
サウルはダビデを宮廷に迎えましたが、後に彼を警戒し、命を狙うようになりました。
サウルはエンドルの女を訪ね、死者を呼び出すよう求めました。
サウルと息子たちはギルボア山で戦死しました。

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: “Go and speak to David, ‘The LORD says, “I offer you three things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.”’”

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: David went up according to the saying of Gad, as the LORD commanded.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Joab the son of Zeruiah and David’s servants went out, and met them by the pool of Gibeon; and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool and the other on the other side of the pool.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Abner said to Joab, “Please let the young men arise and compete before us!” Joab said, “Let them arise!”

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was as light of foot as a wild gazelle.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Abner said again to Asahel, “Turn away from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I look Joab your brother in the face?”
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. The sun went down when they had come to the hill of Ammah, that lies before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, “Shall the sword devour forever? Don’t you know that it will be bitterness in the latter end? How long will it be then, before you ask the people to return from following their brothers?”
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Joab said, “As God lives, if you had not spoken, surely then in the morning the people would have gone away, and not each followed his brother.”
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: So Joab blew the trumpet; and all the people stood still and pursued Israel no more, and they fought no more.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Joab returned from following Abner; and when he had gathered all the people together, nineteen men of David’s and Asahel were missing.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: They took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father, which was in Bethlehem. Joab and his men went all night, and the day broke on them at Hebron.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Behold, David’s servants and Joab came from a raid and brought in a great plunder with them; but Abner was not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: When Joab and all the army who was with him had come, they told Joab, “Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he has sent him away, and he has gone in peace.”
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then Joab came to the king and said, “What have you done? Behold, Abner came to you. Why is it that you have sent him away, and he is already gone?
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: When Joab had come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah; but David didn’t know it.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Let it fall on the head of Joab and on all his father’s house. Let there not fail from the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or who is a leper, or who leans on a staff, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks bread.”

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your clothes, and clothe yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn in front of Abner.” King David followed the bier.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel and put them in array against the Syrians.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: So Joab and the people who were with him came near to the battle against the Syrians, and they fled before him.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: At the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, David sent Joab and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: David sent to Joab, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” Joab sent Uriah to David.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: When Uriah had come to him, David asked him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then David said to the messenger, “Tell Joab, ‘Don’t let this thing displease you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Make your battle stronger against the city, and overthrow it.’ Encourage him.”

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Joab sent messengers to David, and said, “I have fought against Rabbah. Yes, I have taken the city of waters.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman from there, and said to her, “Please act like a mourner, and put on mourning clothing, please, and don’t anoint yourself with oil; but be as a woman who has mourned a long time for the dead.
primaryWitnessAudit.verificationMethod: source-ID/URL/knownBy resolved to pinned WEB coordinate; fixed text re-read

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Go in to the king and speak like this to him.” So Joab put the words in her mouth.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: The king said, “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?” The woman answered, “As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab urged me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your servant.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Your servant Joab has done this thing to change the face of the matter. My lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are on the earth.”

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

primaryWitnessAudit.fixedWEBText: Then Joab arose and came to Absalom to his house, and said to him, “Why have your servants set my field on fire?”

factGates.textJa: ダビデとその部下たちは、サウルとヨナタン、イスラエルの民が剣に倒れたことを悼みました。
アブネルはサウルの子イシュ・ボシェテをマハナイムへ連れて行き、イスラエルの王としました。
ヨナタンの子メフィボシェトは、サウル家の土地を受け継ぐ者として記されます。
サウル家のシムイはダビデを呪い、後に赦しを求めました。
